BINTSHATI:v1p154/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r7.claim: The author prefers the verbal-noun reading as broader: the human will remember his striving, echoing the statement that each person has only what he strove for.
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r7.anchor: والذي نراه أن المصدرة أعم وأولى بالمقام، فيكون المعنى: يوم يتذكر الإنسان مسعاه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.claim: Islahi wonders at people who boast of Abrahamic or Mosaic association and expect high rank while withholding charity, since those scriptures teach that no one bears another's burden and each faces the fruit of his own deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.anchor: the most prominent teaching of Abraham (sws) and Moses (sws) was that in the Hereafter no one will bear the burden of another person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r4.claim: Each person receives only what they strive for; a pious ancestor’s reward does not transfer to descendants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r4.anchor: no soul will be rewarded for the virtues of another or punished for the misdeeds of someone else

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r5.claim: Noah’s son, Abraham’s father, and Lot’s wife could not benefit from their prophetic relatives, while Pharaoh’s wife is praised in 66:11.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r5.anchor: even the closest relations of a prophet whose record was devoid of good deeds were not able to benefit from this relationship

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r6.claim: A person’s good deed benefiting another must rest on their affectionate relationship of faith.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r6.anchor: this good deed should be based on a person’s affectionate relationship of faith with another person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r1.claim: A person also shares in another’s good deed through a direct or indirect role, such as teaching, serving as an example, or financial help.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r1.anchor: a believer taught a believer or became an exemplar of a teaching for the other person or had financially helped the other person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r2.speaker: Some people having a socialistic mentality
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r2.claim: They read the verse as requiring earnings proportionate to labor; Islahi rejects this as unrelated to the context and a misuse of intelligence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r2.anchor: that a person should earn what is commensurate to the work he put in

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r3.claim: Worldly provision is distributed to test gratitude and patience, while the Hereafter settles matters through justice and earned reward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r3.anchor: He has blessed some abundantly and some stringently and in this manner tested the gratefulness and patience of both.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r4.claim: Those who pass the worldly trial are rewarded for their deeds; those who fail receive no reward and go to Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r4.anchor: people who pass this trial will be rewarded for their good deeds

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r5.claim: On the apparent reading, “man” includes believer and unbeliever, and the restriction means each has no effort other than his own.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r5.anchor: الظاهر أن الإنسان يشمل المؤمن والكافر، وأن الحصر في السعي، فليس له سعي غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r6.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r6.claim: ʿIkrima says this rule applied to the communities of Abraham and Moses, while this community can benefit from others' efforts, as the Prophet's answer to Saʿd ibn ʿUbada shows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r6.anchor: وقال عكرمة: كان هذا الحكم في قوم إبراهيم وموسى، وأما هذه الأمة فلها سعي غيرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r7.speaker: سعد بن عبادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r7.claim: Saʿd asked whether his mother would benefit if he gave charity for her, and the Prophet answered yes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r7.anchor: يدل عليه حديث سعد بن عبادة: هل لأمي، إن تطوعت عنها؟ قال: نعم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r8.speaker: الربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r8.claim: Al-Rabiʿ takes “man” here to mean the unbeliever; the believer receives his own effort and what others do for him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r8.anchor: وقال الربيع: الإنسان هنا الكافر، وأما المؤمن فله ما سعى وما سعى له غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r9.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r9.claim: Husayn ibn al-Fadl answers that justice grants a person only what he strove for, while grace grants whatever God wills, reconciling the verse with God's multiplying reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r9.anchor: فقال: ليس له بالعدل إلا ما سعى، وله بالفضل ما شاء الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r10.claim: The report that Ibn Abbas considered this verse abrogated is unsound, since the report does not convey a legal obligation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r10.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس أنها منسوخة لا يصح، لأنه خبر لم يتضمن تكليفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r11.claim: The majority hold that the verse remains definitive and un-abrogated.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the key is the phrase “for man”: strictly speaking, a person can claim as his own only his own effort; benefits from others or divine grace are not literally his due.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r12.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والتحرير عندي في هذه الآية أن ملاك المعنى هو اللام من قوله: للإنسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r13.claim: Some use the verse to argue that nobody can perform bodily or financial acts for another after death; other scholars distinguish bodily acts from financial ones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r13.anchor: واحتج بهذه الآية من يرى أنه لا يعمل أحد عن أحد بعد موته ببدن أو مال، وفرق بعض العلماء بين البدن والمال

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.claim: This section then turns to perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.anchor: transitions into a discussion of the perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham

RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.claim: The most apparent content is the rule that no bearer carries another's burden, though the phrase may cover more because the scrolls contain more than this alone.
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.anchor: هو ما ذكر بقوله : { ألا تزر

RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.claim: Rāzī explains Abraham's fulfillment by saying he kept his promise to seek forgiveness for his father and did so; God's refusal taught that each person receives only the fruits of his own effort and no soul bears another's sin.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.anchor: فاستغفر ووفى بالعهد ولم يغفر الله له

RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r1.claim: This completes the account of accountability: just as another cannot carry one's sin, another's good deed does not benefit one who did no good and cannot supply him a reward.
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r1.anchor: أن سيئته لا يتحملها عنه أحد بين له أن حسنة الغير لا تجدي نفعا

RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r2.claim: Rāzī holds الإنسان to be general, despite objections that relatives' charity, fasting, and prayer benefit the dead and that tenfold reward exceeds the deed.
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r2.anchor: أنه عام وهو الحق وقيل عليه بأن في الأخبار أن ما يأتي به القريب من الصدقة والصوم يصل إلى الميت

RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r3.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r3.claim: An objection cites unspecified reports that a close relative's charity and fasting reach the dead, and says prayer also benefits them; no report authority is named here.
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r3.anchor: في الأخبار أن ما يأتي به القريب من الصدقة والصوم يصل إلى الميت والدعاء أيضا نافع

RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r4.claim: Rāzī answers that the deceased receives a relative's charity only through his own effort of faith; the tenfold increase is also within what one seeks by doing good in hope of God's promised generosity.
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r4.anchor: إن الإنسان إن لم يسع في أن يكون له صدقة القريب بالإيمان لا يكون له صدقته

RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r5.claim: Though سعى usually means performed work, not merely seeking a thing (which would take فيه), the verse refers to the work's reward or to the deed preserved for its agent, not necessarily the deed itself.
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r5.anchor: لا بد من زيادة فإن قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r6.claim: The view that الإنسان here means only the unbeliever is weak.
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r6.anchor: أن المراد من الإنسان الكافر دون المؤمن وهو ضعيف

RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r7.claim: Rāzī rejects the claim that this rule belonged to an earlier law and was abrogated in Muhammad's law, where people supposedly receive what they did not earn; he says the proposed abrogation is needless.
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r7.anchor: وهو باطل إذ لا حاجة إلى هذا التكلف

RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r8.claim: On the literal reading, a person's work remains محفوظ with God without loss and is then requited, as 99:7 says that whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.
RAZI-FULL:v29p14/r8.anchor: له عين ما سعى محفوظ عند الله تعالى ولا نقصان يدخله ثم يجزى به

RAZI-FULL:v29p14#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p14#2/r2.speaker: المشهور
RAZI-FULL:v29p14#2/r2.claim: The well-known reading includes every deed: good deeds are rewarded and evil deeds punished.
RAZI-FULL:v29p14#2/r2.anchor: المشهور أنهما لكل عمل فالخير مثاب عليه والشر معاقب به

RAZI-FULL:v29p14#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p14#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p14#2/r3.claim: Rāzī says the apparent point is benefits from good deeds: لام marks what is for a person, unlike على for what is against him; full recompense fits good, while evil may be matched, lessened, or forgiven.
RAZI-FULL:v29p14#2/r3.anchor: والظاهر أنه لبيان الخيرات يدل عليه اللام

RAZI-FULL:v29p14#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p14#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p14#2/r4.claim: The past tense سعى encourages good works: future promises to pray or give are not yet earned or recorded, so the verse says a person has only what he has already done.

STUDYQURAN:53:39/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:39/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:39/r1.claim: As no one bears another’s sins, no one is rewarded for good deeds another person performed.
STUDYQURAN:53:39/r1.anchor: Just as none will bear the sins of another, so too will none be rewarded for the good deeds performed by another.

STUDYQURAN:53:39/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:39/r2.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:53:39/r2.claim: A famous hadith says a person’s deeds end at death except a righteous child’s supplication, continuing charity, and knowledge that benefits others.
STUDYQURAN:53:39/r2.anchor: When a person dies, his deeds are cut off, save for three things: a righteous child who makes supplication for him

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r7.claim: An is again the lightened emphatic particle; li-l-insān is the predicate of laysa, while mā saʿā is its subject, verbal noun or relative clause.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r7.anchor: إن مخففة من الثقيلة كأختها معطوفة عليها وللإنسان خبر ليس وإلا ما سعى اسمها

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r8.claim: Saʿy is brisk walking, less than running, and by extension earnest effort in a matter, good or evil.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r8.anchor: والسعي المشي الذريع وهو دون العدو ويستعمل للجد في الأمر خيرا كان أو شرا

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r9.claim: In the afterlife a person has only his own worldly work and intention; as no one avoids harm through another's deed, one does not gain that deed's reward either.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r9.anchor: والمعنى وأنه أي الشأن ليس للإنسان في الآخرة إلا سعيه في الدنيا من العمل والنية

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to deny reward for another's effort, a rule Bursevī says is abrogated for this community: children benefit from righteous parents and family members intercede for one another.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r10.anchor: فروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عدم إثابة الإنسان بسعي غيره وفعله وهذا منسوخ الحكم في هذه الشريعة

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r11.speaker: عكرمة
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r11.claim: ʿIkrima says the restriction applied to Abraham's and Moses' peoples, while this community receives its own effort and what others do for it.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r11.anchor: قال عكرمة : كان ذلك لقوم إبراهيم وموسى وأما هذه الأمة فلهم ما سعوا وما سعى لهم غيرهم

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r12.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r12.claim: The Prophet told a woman that her infant would receive pilgrimage and she would be rewarded; he also affirmed reward when a man gave charity for his suddenly deceased mother.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r12.anchor: وقال رجل للنبي عليه السلام : إن أمي افتلتت نفسها أي ماتت فجأة فهل لها أجر إن تصدقت عنها

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r13.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r13.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas says the exclusion concerns unbelievers; a believer receives his effort and effort performed for him by others.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r13.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس وإن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى يعني الكافر وأما المؤمن فعله ما سعى

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r14.claim: Bursevī says many reports support the view that a believer receives reward for another person's good deed.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r14.anchor: وكثير من الأحاديث يدل على هذا القول ويشهد له أن المؤمن يصل إليه ثواب العمل الصالح من غيره

BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r1.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r1.claim: Al-Baqlī says the human form earns through deeds purified of ostentation; their reward is Paradise, while vision and closeness are gifts of divine grace to the spirit beyond earned recompense.
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r1.anchor: قال البقلي رحمه الله في تأويل الآية ليس للصورة الانسانية الا ما سعت من الاعمال الزكية عن الرياء والسمعة

BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r2.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r2.claim: After the soul receives earned Paradise levels, it may also enjoy God's grace in lifting the veil of His beauty; witnessing and intimacy remain gifts God gives as He wills.
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r2.anchor: فانه إذا استوفى درجات الجنان التي هي جزآء اعماله الصالحة تمتع ايضا بما يجد روحه من فضل الله

BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says a person gets from striving only what he intended: divine pleasure for striving toward God, or reward and compensation when those were the aims.
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء ليس للانسان من سعيه الا ما نواه ان كان سعيه لرضى الرحمن

BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r4.speaker: النصر ابادي
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r4.claim: Al-Naṣrābādhī says the seeker strives while traveling the path, but at realization still strives without acting from his separate self.
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r4.anchor: وقال النصر ابادي سعى الانسان في طريق السلوك لا في طريق التحقيق فاذا تحقق يسعى ولا يسعى هو بنفسه

BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r5.claim: Jāmī's couplet says travelers cannot arrive without the Friend's attraction, even after years of exertion.
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r5.anchor: سالكان بي كشش دوست بجايي نرسند

BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r6.claim: Bursevī says the couplet does not contradict the verse: effort belongs to the seeker and divine attraction to God, but neither helps without the other; at realization both belong to God.
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r6.anchor: فانه لا فائدة في السعي بدون الجذبة الالهية فالسعي منسوب الى السالك والجذبة مضافة الى الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r7.claim: The path is one in its unity though paths to God are as numerous as creatures' breaths; they converge at the end, and after death God brings the seeker to his aspiration.
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r7.anchor: والا فالطرق الى الله بعدد انفاس الخلائق فعند النهاية يحصل الالتقاء ولذا قال تعالى وان الى ربك المنهى

BURSEVI:v9p207/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p207/r4.speaker: الوراق
BURSEVI:v9p207/r4.claim: Al-Warrāq maps striving to beginning, middle, and end; at the end, annihilation is rewarded with witnessing and subsistence with bodily nurture, including lawful provisions deferred during the path.
BURSEVI:v9p207/r4.anchor: قالل الوراق : وإن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى ذلك في بدايته وإن سعيه سوف يرى

TABATABAI:53:38-39/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r5.claim: This verse and the following scriptural statements introduced by ‘that’ belong to the set of seventeen verses drawn from the two scriptures.
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r5.anchor: وكذا سائر الآيات المصدرة بأن وأن إلى تمام سبع عشرة آية

TABATABAI:53:38-39/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r6.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r6.claim: Al-Raghib says sa‘y literally means brisk walking, less than running, and is used metaphorically for earnest effort in good or evil.
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r6.anchor: قال الراغب السعي المشي السريع وهو دون العدو، ويستعمل للجد في الأمر خيرا كان أو شرا

TABATABAI:53:38-39/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r7.claim: The lām of ‘for the human being’ denotes true ownership: a lasting possession whose effects remain with its owner.
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r7.anchor: ومعنى اللام في قوله { للإنسان } الملك الحقيقي الذي يقوم بصاحبه قياما باقيا ببقائه

TABATABAI:53:38-39/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r8.claim: Worldly wealth, children, status, and ornaments are only conventional possessions that leave a person at death; truly beneficial or harmful property is what one earns through one’s own good or bad work, not another’s deeds.
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r8.anchor: فكل ذلك من الملك الاعتباري الوهمي الذي يصاحب الإنسان ما دام في دار الغرور

TABATABAI:53:40-43/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r1.claim: Earlier discussions of the verse are connected to the record of people’s deeds and their traces, concern for descendants, and God’s distinguishing the bad from the good.

TABATABAI:53:33-62/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r1.speaker: رواية غير مسماة
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r1.claim: An unnamed report says the deceased knows a deed was done for him; even for a nāṣib it gives some benefit by lightening his burden.
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r1.anchor: قلت وإن كان ناصبا ينفعه ذلك؟ قال نعم يخفف عنه

TABATABAI:53:33-62/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r2.claim: The preceding report concerns gifting the reward of a deed, not performing the deed as a proxy for the deceased.
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r2.anchor: مورد الرواية إهداء ثواب العمل دون العمل نيابة عن الميت

TABATABAI:53:33-62/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r3.claim: The Prophet reports that God tells the angel assigned to a believer to record during illness the deeds that were recorded in health, since God has placed the believer in His care.
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن سنان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:53:33-62/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r4.claim: Imam al-Sadiq says three rewards continue after death: ongoing charity, a rightly guided practice followed by others, and a righteous child’s prayer for the deceased.
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r4.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال ليس يتبع الرجل بعد موته من الأجر إلا ثلاث خصال صدقة أجراها في حياته

TABATABAI:53:33-62/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r5.claim: These reports, along with many similar reports from the Imams, broaden the meaning of a person’s striving to include deeds whose reward or effects continue through others.
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r5.anchor: أقول وهذه الروايات الثلاث - وفي معناها روايات كثيرة جدا عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام

TABRISI:53:32-39/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r16.claim: This clause is joined to the preceding teaching and also belongs to the pages of Moses and Abraham: a person earns only the reward for their own work, not another's.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r16.anchor: عطف على قوله ألا تزر وهذا أيضا ما في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

TABRISI:53:32-39/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r17.claim: If someone calls another to faith and the person responds, the caller is praised derivatively because the caller's own effort caused it; without one's own work there is no earned reward or punishment.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r17.anchor: ومتى دعا غيره إلى الإيمان فأجابه إليه فهو محمود على ذلك

TABRISI:53:32-39/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:53:32-39/r18.claim: In al-Wālibī's transmission, Ibn ʿAbbās says this ruling was abrogated in Islamic law because 52:21 raises descendants' rank although they did not earn it through their own deeds.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r18.anchor: عن ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي قال إن هذا منسوخ الحكم في شريعتنا

TABRISI:53:40-41/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:40-41/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:40-41/r1.claim: The linked verse says God raises the descendants in rank although they did not earn it by their deeds; Ibn Abbas cites it as evidence that the prior ruling was abrogated.
TABRISI:53:40-41/r1.anchor: رفع درجة الذرية وإن لم يستحقوها بأعمالهم

TABRISI:53:40-41/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:40-41/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:53:40-41/r2.claim: ʿIkrima similarly confines the rule to the communities of Abraham and Moses; this community can benefit from others' efforts performed on its behalf.
TABRISI:53:40-41/r2.anchor: نحو هذا قال عكرمة إن ذلك لقوم إبراهيم وموسى فأما هذه الأمة

TABRISI:53:40-41/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:40-41/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:40-41/r3.claim: On the view that the ruling remains, the verse bars deputation in acts of worship except where evidence permits it, such as pilgrimage.
TABRISI:53:40-41/r3.anchor: ومن قال إنه غير منسوخ الحكم قال الآية تدل على منع النيابة في الطاعات

TABRISI:53:40-41/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:40-41/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:53:40-41/r4.claim: A woman said her father had not performed pilgrimage, and the Prophet told her to perform it for him.
TABRISI:53:40-41/r4.anchor: أن امرأة قالت يا رسول الله أن أبي لم يحج

TABRISI:53:44-51/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:44-51/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:44-51/r15.claim: The clauses opened with anna are all treated as teachings in the pages of Abraham and Moses, following the report of what those pages contain.
TABRISI:53:44-51/r15.anchor: وإنما فتحت أن في هذه المواضع كلها لأن جميعها في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

THALABI:v9p153/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p153/r1.claim: The person's striving means his deeds.
THALABI:v9p153/r1.anchor: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى أي عمل

THALABI:v9p153/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p153/r2.claim: The commentary compares this statement about striving with the verse saying people's striving differs.
THALABI:v9p153/r2.anchor: نظيره قوله سبحانه: إن سعيكم لشتى

THALABI:v9p153/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p153/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās considers the verse abrogated by the promise that believing descendants will be joined to their righteous forebears, entering Paradise through their fathers' righteousness.
THALABI:v9p153/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذه الآية منسوخة، فأنزل الله بعدها والذين آمنوا واتبعتهم ذريتهم بإيمان ألحقنا بهم ذرياتهم

THALABI:v9p153/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r4.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v9p153/r4.claim: ʿIkrima restricts the rule to the communities of Abraham and Moses; this community receives the benefit of its own striving and that of others.
THALABI:v9p153/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: كان ذلك لقوم إبراهيم وموسى، فأما هذه الأمة فلهم ما سعوا وما سعى غيرهم

THALABI:v9p153/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p153/r5.claim: A report says the Prophet allowed a questioner to give voluntary charity on behalf of his mother, supporting benefit from another person's action.
THALABI:v9p153/r5.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: هل لأمي إن تطوعت عنها؟

THALABI:v9p153/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p153/r6.claim: When a woman said her father had died without performing pilgrimage, the Prophet told her to perform it on his behalf.
THALABI:v9p153/r6.anchor: المرأة التي سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت: إن أبي مات ولم يحج

THALABI:v9p153/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
THALABI:v9p153/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas takes “the person” to mean an unbeliever; a believer receives reward for his own striving and that of others.
THALABI:v9p153/r7.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: وأن ليس للإنسان يعني الكافر، فأما المؤمن فله ما سعى وما سعي

THALABI:v9p153/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p153/r8.claim: Another view says an unbeliever receives only the good he did, and is repaid for it in worldly life so no good remains for him in the afterlife.
THALABI:v9p153/r8.anchor: وقيل: ليس للكافر من الخير إلا ما عمله فيثاب عليه في دار الدنيا حتى لا يبقى له في الآخرة خير

THALABI:v9p153/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي
THALABI:v9p153/r9.claim: A report says ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy gave al-ʿAbbās a shirt; after Ubayy's death the Prophet sent his own shirt to shroud him, leaving Ubayy no good deed for afterlife reward.
THALABI:v9p153/r9.anchor: ويروى أن عبد الله بن أبي كان أعطى العباس قميصا ألبسه إياه، فلما مات عبد الله أرسل رسول الله قميصه ليكفن فيه

THALABI:v9p153/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r10.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v9p153/r10.claim: The governor ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāhir invited al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl to resolve three apparent contradictions: Cain's regret and repentance, God's daily activity and the dried Pen, and how reward can exceed one's striving.
THALABI:v9p153/r10.anchor: دعا عبد الله بن طاهر والي خراسان الحسين بن الفضل قال: أشكلت علي ثلاث آيات دعوتك لتكشفها لي

THALABI:v9p153/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r11.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v9p153/r11.claim: Al-Ḥusayn allows that Cain's regret was not repentance, whereas this community's regret is repentance; God gave this community distinctive privileges.
THALABI:v9p153/r11.anchor: قال الحسين: يجوز ان لا يكون ندم قابيل توبة له، ويكون ندم هذه الأمة توبة لها، إن الله سبحانه خص هذه الأمة بخصائص

THALABI:v9p153/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p153/r12.claim: Another explanation says Cain regretted having to carry Abel's body, rather than regretting the killing.
THALABI:v9p153/r12.anchor: وفيه قول آخر: وهو أن ندم قابيل لم يكن على قتل هابيل، وإنما كان على حمله

THALABI:v9p153/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p153/r14.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v9p153/r14.claim: Al-Ḥusayn reads the verse as describing what a person earns by justice; God may then multiply one deed a thousandfold by grace.
THALABI:v9p153/r14.anchor: وأما قوله: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى يعني عن طريق العدل، ومجاز الآية: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى عدلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r1.claim: This clause is coordinated with “that none bears another’s burden” and is also among the teachings in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r1.anchor: قوله: {وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى} عطف على قوله: {ألا تزر}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r2.claim: Muqātil reads it as allowing a person in the afterlife only what that person did in worldly life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى: ليس للإنسان في الآخرة إلا ما عمل في الدنيا، قاله مقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains that a person receives only the recompense of their striving: good for good and evil for evil; al-Wāḥidī calls this the apparent meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: معناه: ليس له إلا جزاء سعيه، إن عمل خيرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r4.speaker: الوالبي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through al-Wālibī, says the rule was abrogated for this community by 52:21: children enter Paradise through their parents’ righteousness and have their ranks raised without earning them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r4.anchor: روى الوالبي عن ابن عباس أن هذا منسوخ الحكم في هذه الشريعة بقوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r5.claim: ʿIkrima says the rule applied to the communities of Abraham and Moses, whereas this community may benefit from others’ deeds performed on its behalf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r5.anchor: ونحو هذا قال عكرمة: كان ذلك لقوم إبراهيم وموسى، فأما هذه الأمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r6.claim: A woman told the Prophet her father died without performing pilgrimage, and he told her to perform it for him, evidence for proxy worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r6.anchor: بدليل حديث المرأة التي قالت لرسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r7.speaker: أصحابنا
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r7.claim: The author’s legal school says the verse bars proxy performance of devotional acts except where evidence permits it, such as pilgrimage, if the rule is not abrogated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r7.anchor: وقال العلماء من أصحابنا: هذه الآية تدل على منع النيابة في الطاعات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r8.claim: The ruling turns on abrogation: without it, proxy worship is barred except for established exceptions; on al-Wālibī and ʿIkrima’s account, it is abrogated in Islamic law.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r8.anchor: وهذا إذا قلنا إنه غير منسوخ الحكم، وعلى ما ذكر الوالبي وعكرمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r9.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥusayn b. al-Faḍl says the verse states justice, while God may graciously multiply good deeds as He wills.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p67#2/r9.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل (¬6): هذا من طريق العدل ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r4.claim: A person has only the work he has done for his Hereafter.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r4.anchor: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى } عمل لآخرته

QASHANI:53:37-39/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:37-39/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:37-39/r3.claim: No one bears another's burden because reward and punishment arise from settled dispositions formed by repeated good or bad acts; immediate allotted fortunes also depend on divine decree, but the proximate cause counts.
QASHANI:53:37-39/r3.anchor: لأن العقاب يترتب على هيئات مظلمة رسخت في النفس بتكرار الأفاعيل والأقاويل السيئة

QASHANI:53:37-39/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:37-39/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:37-39/r4.claim: The next life has three returns: bodily resurrection for judgment, return to primordial nature and the heart, and return to gifted Real existence after complete annihilation; only the first is universal.
QASHANI:53:37-39/r4.anchor: النشأة الأخرى تقع على أمور ثلاثة

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r5.claim: A person is not entitled as their own to reward from another's striving, just as they are not liable for another's crime; another's gift may still be donated to them.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r5.anchor: Yani bir insan başkasının cürmü ile muâhaze olunmayacağı gibi kendi sa‘yinden başkasıyla sevablanmak da kendinin has hakkı değildir.

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r6.claim: The rule is aligned with 2:286, which assigns each soul what it earns and against it what it acquires.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r6.anchor: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r7.claim: The verse cannot mean that people receive nothing beyond their own effort, since divine gifts and mercy reach them, and cooperation is commanded and beneficial.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r7.anchor: insana gerek dünyada olsun gerek âhirette sa‘y ü kesbinden başka vehbî olarak verilen nice rahmet ve atâyâ-yı ilâhiye bulunduğunda da şüphe yoktur.

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r8.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r8.claim: Benefits from prophets' intercession, angels' prayers for forgiveness, and the living's prayers or charity for the dead rest on the recipient's own faith and righteousness; without faith they do not benefit.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r8.anchor: Ebussuud der ki: “Enbiyânın şefaati, melâikenin istiğfârı, dirilerin ölüler için duası, sadakası gibi

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r9.speaker: Hüseyin b. Fazl
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r9.claim: Asked by Abdullah ibn Tahir about 2:261 and this verse, Husayn ibn Fadl replied that justice gives only what one strove for, while grace gives as much as God wills; the governor kissed his head.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r9.anchor: Hüseyin ona “adl ile ancak mâ-se‘â, fazl ile ise Allah’ın dilediği kadar vardır” diye cevap verdi

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r10.claim: The verse is consistent with 52:21, which says every person is held for what they earned.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r10.anchor: Sûre-i Tûr’a bak كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍۭ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينٌۭ

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r11.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r11.claim: The report that Ibn Abbas called this verse abrogated is not sound; the majority holds the verse definitive and unabrogated.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r11.anchor: Bunun mensuh olduğuna dair İbn Abbas’tan söylenen söz sahih değildir.

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r12.speaker: İbn Atıyye
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r12.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the lām is the pivot: only one's own striving is truly one's due; intercession, righteous relatives' care, multiplied good deeds, and pure grace are mercy, not one's property or entitlement, except metaphorically.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r12.anchor: İbn Atıyye bunu şöyle tahkik eder: “Bence bu âyette tahrir şöyledir: Mânanın mihveri لِلْإِنسَٰنِ’daki lâmdır.

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r13.claim: The lām indicates اختصاص or entitlement, and the restriction focuses on that relation; ma is primarily a verbal noun meaning striving, though it may be relative, since not everything a person strives for becomes theirs.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r13.anchor: “Mâ-se‘â”daki مَا masdariyyedir, sa‘y demektir, sa‘y ettiği mânasına mevsûle olması ihtimâli de melhuz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r3.claim: People must make voluntary choices within a testing order whose full secrets and subtleties are beyond human knowledge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r3.anchor: Herkes bütün sırlarını ve inceliklerini bilemeyeceğimiz bir sınav düzeni içinde iradî seçimler yapmak durumundadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r7.claim: These verses also affirm the value before God of honest effort and earning through one’s own labor.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r7.anchor: dürüstlükle çalışıp çabalamanın, alın teriyle kazanmanın Allah nezdindeki değerine de işaret etmektedir

SULAMI:v2p288/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p288/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p288/r1.claim: A person has only what he repudiates of his striving and disclaims as his own.
SULAMI:v2p288/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : ليس للإنسان إلا ما جحد من سعيه وتبرأ منه

SULAMI:v2p288/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p288/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p288/r2.claim: A person receives according to the intention behind striving: seeking the Merciful’s pleasure brings His approval, while seeking reward or compensation brings that return.
SULAMI:v2p288/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : ليس له من سعيه إلا ما نواه إن كان سعيه لرضا الرحمن فإن الله يرزقه الرضوان

SULAMI:v2p288/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p288/r3.speaker: محمد بن عيسى الهاشمي
SULAMI:v2p288/r3.claim: The safest route is to know oneself and restrain it from its desires, since desires account for most of its striving.
SULAMI:v2p288/r3.anchor: قال محمد بن عيسى الهاشمي : اقرب الطريق من السلامة معرفة المرء بنفسه ومنعها من شهواتها

SULAMI:v2p288/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p288/r4.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v2p288/r4.claim: Striving belongs to the path of spiritual wayfaring, not the path of Reality; upon realization, the servant is carried by God rather than moving by himself. His poem says Truth’s path is single and its travelers are rare.
SULAMI:v2p288/r4.anchor: قال النصرآباذي : سعى الإنسان في طريق السلوك لا في طريق الحقيقة فإذا تحقق سعى به ولا يسعى

SULAMI:v2p288/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p288/r5.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v2p288/r5.claim: Two seekers differ greatly: one seeks a path to see the kingdom, the other a path to witness the King; a poem voices longing to meet the beloved alone.
SULAMI:v2p288/r5.anchor: سمعت النصرآباذي يقول : ساع يسعى في طريق ليرى فيه المملكة وساع يسعى في طريق ليشهد فيه الملك

SULAMI:v2p288/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p288/r6.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v2p288/r6.claim: Al-Warraq maps striving to the beginner’s stage, its being seen to the middle stage, full recompense to the final stage, the end toward God to the servant’s annihilation from will and attributes, and laughter and weeping to a second arising.
SULAMI:v2p288/r6.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق في قوله : ﴿ وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى ﴾ ذلك في بداياتهم

ITQAN:v1p296#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p296#2/r1.speaker: الأئمة الثلاثة
ITQAN:v1p296#2/r1.claim: The three other major imams hold that the reward of Qur'an recitation can reach the deceased.
ITQAN:v1p296#2/r1.anchor: الأئمة الثلاثة على وصول ثواب القراءة للميت ومذهبنا خلافه

ITQAN:v1p296#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p296#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p296#2/r2.claim: The author's school disagrees, citing the verse's statement that a person has only what they strove for as evidence against the reward of recitation reaching the dead.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r1.speaker: هذه الطائفة
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r1.claim: The group dismisses poetry as frivolous material such as jokes, ruins, camels, and excessive praise or satire, with no need for religious or worldly well-being.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r1.anchor: أما الشعر فخيل إليها أنه ليس فيه كثير طائل ، وأن ليس إلا ملحة أو فكاهة أو بكاء منزل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r2.speaker: هذه الطائفة
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r2.claim: The group treats advanced grammar as artificial and baseless, claiming that only elementary knowledge of case endings is useful.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r2.anchor: وأما النحو فظنته ضربا من التكلف ، وبابا من التعسف ، وشيئا لا يستند إلى أصل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r3.claim: Recognizing the Qurʾān’s inimitability requires knowledge of Arabic poetry and the causes of its degrees of excellence, since the Qurʾān’s proof rests on eloquence beyond human reach.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r3.anchor: وكان محالا أن يعرف كونه كذلك إلا من عرف الشعر الذي هو ديوان العرب

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r4.claim: Al-Jurjānī condemns choosing ignorance of these disciplines as obstructing God’s path and seeking to extinguish God’s light.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p24/r4.anchor: بإيثارهم الجهل بذلك على العلم في معنى الصاد عن سبيل الله ، والمبتغي إطفاء نور الله تعالى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p65/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p65/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p65/r1.claim: Al-Jurjānī concludes that rhetorical merit belongs to meanings rather than words and is perceived through thought and reason; he now proposes to detail the grounds on which that merit arises.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p65/r1.anchor: قد فرغنا الآن من الكلام على جنس المزية ، وأنها من حيز المعاني دون الألفاظ ، وأنها ليست لك حيث تسمع بأذنك ، بل حيث تنظر بقلبك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p214/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p214/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p214/r1.claim: When context shows the act eventually occurred despite seeming unlikely, ما كادوا يفعلون means they nearly failed to do it; the author distinguishes this from absolute non-occurrence.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p214/r1.anchor: المعنى على أنك تزعم أن الفعل لم يقارب أن يكون

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p214/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p214/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p214/r2.claim: In the poem, لم يرها ولم يكد denies that seeing even approached occurrence; it does not mean that seeing happened after nearly failing to happen.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p214/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p214/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p214/r3.claim: Because لم يكد occurs as the answer to إذا, its past form has future force; reading it as an already completed act would make the conditional incoherent.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p214/r3.anchor: والماضي إذا وقع في جواب الشرط على هذا السبيل كان مستقبلا في المعنى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r1.claim: Rhetorical discourse can be appreciated only by listeners with taste and expertise who notice changes in their response and recognize a merit when it is pointed out.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r1.anchor: وحتى يكون ممن تحدثه نفسه بأن لما يومىء إليه من الحسن واللطف أصلا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r2.claim: Someone who sees only grammatical correctness and overt parsing resembles a person without the sense of poetic meter, and lacks the faculty needed to benefit from explanation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r2.anchor: فأما من كانت الحالان والوجهان عنده أبدا على سواء وكان لا يفقه من أمر النظم إلا الصحة المطلقة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r3.claim: The claim that rhetorical causes cannot be understood is intellectual laziness; investigate whatever causes can be known and use them as evidence for further inquiry.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r3.anchor: وإن قل فتجعله شاهدا فيما لم تعرف أحرى من أن تسد باب المعرفة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r4.speaker: الجاحظ
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r4.claim: Al-Jahiz warns that the saying that earlier scholars left nothing for later scholars would damage learning if it stopped later generations from investigating.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p224/r4.anchor: قال الجاحظ : ' وكلام كثير قد جرى على ألسنة الناس

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r1.claim: The cited poems serve as evidence against locating inimitability in pleasant letter sounds or ease of pronunciation: the poets' own descriptions concern poetic craft and meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r1.anchor: حتى إن حمل حامل نفسه على الغرر والتقحم على غير بصيرة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r2.claim: Tamim's rugged-mountain image and Adi's measuring and straightening of poetry evoke shaping a poem, not merely choosing letters that are light on the tongue.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r2.anchor: لأن تسلم ألفاظه من حروف تثقل على اللسان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r3.claim: Bashshar's image of eye-light sinking into the heart, alongside the sought pearl and rain of minds, treats poetry as an intellectual treasure rather than phonetic ease.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r3.anchor: وأن يكون اللؤلؤ الذي كان لا ينام عن طلبه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p376/r4.claim: Al-Buhturi's comparison of composing poetry to David making mail exemplifies deliberate craft and measured arrangement.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#6/r1.claim: A person has only what he has done for his Hereafter.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#6/r1.anchor: {وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى} أي ما عمل لآخرته.

NAHHAS:v4p276/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p276/r8.claim: This clause continues the preceding series of statements introduced by anna.

NAHHAS:v4p276/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p276/r9.claim: A person is recompensed only for what that person has done.
NAHHAS:v4p276/r9.anchor: أي لا يجازي إنسان إلا بما عمل

SAMIN-DURR:53:39-40/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:39-40/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:39-40/r1.claim: أن is lightened and is not separated from ليس because ليس is nonconjugating.
SAMIN-DURR:53:39-40/r1.anchor: هي المخففة أيضا. ولم يفصل هنا بينها وبين الفعل لأنه لا يتصرف.

SAMIN-DURR:53:39-40/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:39-40/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:39-40/r2.claim: Both وأن clauses may be genitive, nominative, or accusative through coordination with the preceding أن.
SAMIN-DURR:53:39-40/r2.anchor: ومحلها الجر أو الرفع أو النصب لعطفها على أن قبلها، وكذلك محل

ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r8.claim: This too is among the teachings in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r8.anchor: أي هذا أيضا مما في صحف إبراهيم وموسى عليهما السلام

ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r9.claim: A person receives only the recompense for his own striving: good for good and evil for evil.
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r9.anchor: ليس للإنسان إلا جزاء سعيه، إن عمل خيرا جزي خيرا

ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n32/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n32/r1.speaker: Prophet
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n32/r1.claim: Asad cites a well-authenticated Prophetic tradition: only conscious intentions determine judgment; Bukhari, Muslim, Tirmidhi, Abu Da'ud, Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hanbal and others transmit it.
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n32/r1.anchor: the basic, extremely well-authenticated saying of the Prophet

ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n32/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n32/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n32/r2.claim: In Qur'anic ethics, action includes deliberate omission and the deliberate voicing of righteous or sinful beliefs: anything consciously intended and expressed by word or deed.
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n32/r2.anchor: comprises also a deliberate omission of actions, whether good or bad

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r1.claim: This explains that a person is not rewarded for another's deed, following the statement that he is not held accountable for another's sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r1.anchor: بيان لعدم إثابة الإنسان بعمل غيره إثر بيان عدم مؤاخذته بذنب غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r2.claim: Wa-anna is coordinated like the preceding wa-anna; mā may be a verbal noun, or a relative pronoun meaning only what he strove to do.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r2.anchor: كأختها السابقة و ( ما ) مصدرية وجوز كونها موصولة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r3.claim: A man asked the Prophet whether his deceased mother would be rewarded if he gave charity for her, since she died suddenly without speaking; the Prophet answered yes.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r3.anchor: ما أخرجه مسلم والبخاري وأبو داود والنسائي عن عائشة أن رجلا قال لرسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r4.claim: A man told the Prophet his sister had vowed to perform pilgrimage but died; the Prophet compared it to paying her debt and said God's debt is more deserving of payment.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : أتى رجل النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فقال : إن أختي نذرت

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r5.claim: One reply is that when another intends an act for someone, that person is like the principal represented by an agent, so the act counts as his by proxy; this relies on figurative usage or combining literal and figurative senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r5.anchor: بأن الغير لما نوى ذلك الفعل له صار بمنزلة الوكيل عنه القائم مقامه شرعأ فكأنه بسعيه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r6.claim: Another reply is that another's act benefits him only when built on his own effort of faith, so it can be treated as his effort.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r6.anchor: بأن سعي غيره لما لم ينفعه إلا مبنيا على سعي نفسه من الأيمان فكأنه سعيه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r7.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r7.claim: A report says al-As ibn Wa'il had vowed one hundred camels before Islam; Hisham sacrificed fifty, and Amr asked the Prophet, who said his father's fasting and charity would benefit him if he had affirmed monotheism.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r7.anchor: ما أخرجه أحمد عن عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده أن العاص بن وائل نذر في الجاهلية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r8.claim: The same reply is offered to the objection that verses promising multiplied reward conflict with the restriction to one's own effort.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r8.anchor: وأنت تعلم ما في الجواب من النظر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r9.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r9.claim: Husayn ibn al-Fadl answered Ibn Tahir that by justice a person has only what he strove for, while by grace God may grant whatever He wills; Ibn Tahir approved him.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r9.anchor: ليس لهبالعدل إلا ما سعى وله بالفضل ما شاء الله تعالى فقبل عبد الله رأس الحسين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r10.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r10.claim: Ikrima says this rule applied to the teachings of Abraham and Moses, whereas people of this community may benefit from another's effort.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r10.anchor: عكرمة : كان هذاالحكمفي قول إبراهيم وموسى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r11.speaker: سعد بن عبادة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r11.claim: Sa'd ibn Ubada asked whether his mother would benefit from voluntary charity given for her, and the Prophet said yes.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r11.anchor: يدل عليه حديث سعد بن عبادة هل لأمي إذا تطوعت عنها قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : نعم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r12.speaker: الربيع
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r12.claim: Al-Rabi takes al-insān, the human, here to mean the unbeliever; a believer receives both his own effort and what others do for him.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r12.anchor: وقال الربيع : الأنسان هنا الكافر وأما المؤمن فله ما سعى وما سعى له غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to say the verse was abrogated by the promise that believing descendants would be joined to their believing ancestors in Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r13.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن الآية منسوخة بقوله تعالى : ( والذين آمنوا واتبعتهم ذرياتهم بإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r14.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r14.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the abrogation report as unsound: this is a report, not a command, and reports are not abrogated.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r14.anchor: أبو حيان رواية النسخ بأنها لا تصح لأن الآية خبر لم تتضمن تكليفاولا نسخ في الأخبار

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r15.claim: An alternative to abrogation is that the report described earlier scriptures and was later specified for this community; that is a qualification of the report, not abrogation.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r15.anchor: تقييد الأخبار لا إلى النسخ إذ حقيقته أن يراد المعنى ثم من بعدذلك ترتفع إرادته

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r16.claim: Reading the lām as ʿalā, meaning against a person, is far from the apparent wording and the context admonishing one who turned away and gave little.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r16.anchor: وقيلأ : اللام بمعنى على أي ليس على الإنسان غير سعيه وهو بعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r17.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r17.claim: Ibn Atiyya's preferred clarification is that a person can truly claim only his own effort; intercession, a righteous relative, or multiplied reward belongs to him only figuratively or by attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r17.anchor: والتحرير عندي في هذه الآية أن ملاك المعنى هو اللام من قوله سبحانه : ( للإنسان )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r18.claim: On this clarification, the verse does not prove the Mu'tazilite claim that gifting any reward to another is void, or the Shafi'i argument that recitation's reward cannot reach the dead.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r18.anchor: استدلال المعتزلة بالآية على أن العبد إذاجعل ثواب عمله أي عمل كان لغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r19.speaker: ابن الهمام
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r19.claim: Ibn al-Humam says Malik and al-Shafi'i distinguish bodily worship from other acts: they deny transfer of pure bodily worship such as prayer and recitation, but accept acts such as charity and pilgrimage.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r19.anchor: قال الإمام ابن الهمام : إن مالكا والشافعيلا يقولان بوصول العبادات البدنية المحضة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r20.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r20.claim: Al-Nawawi says the well-known Shafi'i position and that of a group is that recitation's reward does not reach the dead; Ahmad and a group of scholars, including some Shafi'is, hold that it does.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r20.anchor: المشهور من مذهب الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه وجماعة أنها لا تصل وذهب أحمد بن حنبل وجماعة من العلماء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r21.claim: The author recommends asking God after recitation to convey its reward to the deceased; he says this suffices outwardly, though some require intention at the beginning.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r21.anchor: فالأختيار أن يقول القاريء بعدفراغه اللهمأوصل ثواب ما قرأنه إلى فلان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r22.claim: He says the reward apparently does not reach the dead when the Qur'an is recited for payment, since the paid recitation earns no reward; payment for teaching is not prohibited.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66#2/r22.anchor: أما غذا كانت بها كما يفعله أكثر الناس اليوم فإنهم يعطون حفظة القرآن أجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r1.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r1.claim: Al-Khafaji says the actual dispute concerns whether another person can perform bodily worship as a proxy and discharge the obligated person's duty, with or without permission and during or after life.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r1.anchor: الخفاجي : هو محتاج إلى التحرير وتحريره أن محل الخلاف العبادة البدنية هل تقبل النيابة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r2.speaker: الطحاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r2.claim: Al-Tahawi says the report that a deceased person’s heir fasts on their behalf belongs to early Islam and was later abrogated; the proxy rule is established for pilgrimage, not fasting.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r2.anchor: فقالأ الطحاوي : إنه كان في صدر الإسلام ثم نسخ

ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r3.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r3.claim: The dispute is not about substitute payments such as feeding, or gifting reward: the latter is a supplication whose acceptance comes through God's grace, like charity for another.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p67/r3.anchor: ليس الكلام في الفدية وإطعام الطعام فإنهبدل وكذا إهداء الثواب سواء كان بعينه أو مثله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r1.claim: Saʿy means deeds, as in 92:4; this teaching also occurs in Abraham and Moses's scrolls.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the ruling is abrogated for this community by 52:21, which admits children to Paradise through their parents' righteousness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هذا منسوخ الحكم في هذه الشريعة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r3.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r3.claim: Ikrima limits the statement to Abraham's and Moses's peoples; this community receives its own efforts and others' efforts on its behalf, as the child pilgrimage report illustrates.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r3.anchor: كان ذلك لقوم إبراهيم وموسى، فأما هذه الأمة فلهم ما سعوا وما سعى لهم غيرهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r4.claim: A woman asks whether her child earns pilgrimage; the Prophet answers yes and says she earns a reward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r4.anchor: فقالت: يا رسول الله ألهذا حج؟ قال: "نعم ولك أجر"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r5.claim: Asked whether charity for his deceased mother would benefit her, the Prophet answers yes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r5.anchor: فهل لها أجر إن تصدقت عنها؟ قال: "نعم"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r6.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says the limitation applies to the unbeliever; a believer receives what he does and what is done for him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r6.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: "وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى" يعني الكافر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r7.claim: Another view says an unbeliever has only the good he did, repaid in this world so no reward remains for the afterlife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r7.anchor: وقيل: ليس للكافر من الخير إلا ما عمل هو، فيثاب عليه في الدنيا حتى لا يبقى له في الآخرة خير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r8.speaker: غير مسمى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r8.claim: An unattributed report says Abd Allah ibn Ubayy gave al-Abbas a shirt; after his death the Prophet sent his own shirt as a shroud, leaving no good deed for afterlife reward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p416/r8.anchor: ويروى أن عبد الله بن أبي كان أعطى العباس قميصا ألبسه إياه، فلما مات أرسل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قميصه

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r1.claim: As no one is punished for another's sin, no one earns reward through another's act; charity or pilgrimage can benefit the dead because the donor intends to act as their deputy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r1.anchor: إلا سعيه أي كما لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب الغير لا يثاب بفعله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r1.claim: A person owns only their effort, but this includes acts arising from love and ties: others’ prayers, proxy Hajj, charity, a child’s acts, and teaching can benefit; this grounds charity for the dead and gifting recitation’s reward.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r1.anchor: ودعاء المؤمنين للمؤمن سعيه بمواددته لهم ولو بموافقته لهم في الدين وكذا الحج عنه والصدقة ونحوهما , وأما الولد فواضح في ذلك

DURR-FULL:v7p661/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the later verse about believing descendants joining their righteous parents qualified this statement: God admits children to Paradise through their parents' righteousness.
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال {وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى} فأنزل الله بعد ذلك (والذين آمنوا واتبعتهم ذريتهم بإيمان ألحقنا بهم ذريتهم)

DURR-FULL:v7p661/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet would recite these verses, then say the istirjaʿ formula and become subdued.
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأ {وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى وأن سعيه سوف يرى ثم يجزاه الجزاء الأوفى} استرجع واستكان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r1.claim: The clause may coordinate with the preceding prepositional phrase, making أن a reduced إنّ, or with the preceding ألا clause, making أن explanatory; either way it reinforces that clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة { ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى } ( النجم : 38 ) ، فيصح أن تكون عطفا على المجرور بالباء فتكون ( أن ) مخففة من الثقيلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r2.claim: Al-insān is a generic noun, and its use under negation makes the statement universal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r2.anchor: وتعريف { الإنسان } تعريف الجنس ، ووقوعه في سياق النفي يفيد العموم ، والمعنى : لا يختص به إلا ما سعاه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r3.claim: Saʿy means work and acquisition; its original sense is walking, transferred to work metaphorically or by metonymy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r3.anchor: والسعي : العمل والاكتساب ، وأصل السعي : المشي ، فأطلق على العمل مجازا مرسلا أو كناية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r4.claim: A person benefits only from his own deeds; the possessive lām favors good deeds as the intended sense, completing the rule that no bearer carries another's burden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r4.anchor: والمعنى : لا تحصل لأحد فائدة عمل إلا ما عمله بنفسه ، فلا يكون له عمل غيره ، ولام الاختصاص يرجح أن المراد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r5.claim: This completes the preceding rule by preventing the inference that only another person's sins are not transferred while that person's good deeds can be received.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r5.anchor: وبذلك يكون ذكر هذا تتميما لمعنى { ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى } ، احتراسا من أن يخطر بالبال أن المدفوع عن غير فاعله هو الوزر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r6.claim: The Qur'an expresses the same principle through Abraham: salvation belongs to the one who comes to God with a sound heart.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r6.anchor: ومعنى الآية محكي في القرآن عن إبراهيم في قوله عنه : { إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r7.claim: As a rule from Abraham's and Moses's laws, binding absent abrogation, one person's act cannot discharge another's individual duty, obligatory or voluntary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r7.anchor: وإذ قد تقرر أن شرع من قبلنا شرع لنا ما لم يرد ناسخ ، تدل هذه الآية على أن عمل أحد لا يجزىء عن أحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r8.claim: Assuming another's financial liability, such as accidental-killing compensation, is different: it is prescribed mutual support.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r8.anchor: وأما تحمل أحد حمالة لفعل فعله غيره مثل ديات القتل الخطأ فذلك من المؤاساة المفروضة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r9.speaker: عكرمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r9.claim: ʿIkrima says this reports an earlier law abrogated for Muslims, so accepting another's deed is a distinctive concession of this community.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r9.anchor: فعن عكرمة أن قوله تعالى : { وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى } حكاية عن شريعة سابقة فلا تلزم في شريعتنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r10.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r10.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas construes “the human” as the unbeliever; a believer receives his own striving and what others strive for him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p132/r10.anchor: وعن الربيع بن أنس أنه تأول ( الإنسان ) في قوله تعالى : { وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى } بالإنسان الكافر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r1.speaker: الباجي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r1.claim: Al-Bājī argues that representation is valid because Mālik enforced a bequest for pilgrimage and required the hired proxy to have made his own pilgrimage first.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r1.anchor: ورجح الباجي القول بصحة النيابة في ذلك بأن مالكا أمضى الوصية بذلك ، وقال : لا يستأجر له إلا من حج عن نفسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r2.speaker: ابن الفرس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r2.claim: Ibn al-Faras says Mālik permits bequeathing the obligatory pilgrimage, counting it as the deceased's own striving.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r2.anchor: قال ابن الفرس : ( أجاز مالك الوصية بالحج الفرض ، ورأى أنه إذا أوصى بذلك فهو من سعيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r3.speaker: الحنفية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r3.claim: The established Ḥanafī position permits a proxy pilgrimage for someone unable, if incapacity lasts until death; recovery requires pilgrimage personally.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r3.anchor: والمحرر من مذهب الحنفية صحة النيابة في الحج لغير القادر بشرط دوام عجزه إلى الموت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r4.claim: Some Mālikī books transmit a different position from Abū Ḥanīfa on proxy pilgrimage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r4.anchor: وقد ينقل عن أبي حنيفة غير ذلك في كتب المالكية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r5.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī permits pilgrimage for a deceased person and bequest for it, though Ibn al-Faras notes one of his opinions forbids it and cites this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r5.anchor: وجوز الشافعي الحج عن الميت ووصية الميت بالحج عنه . قال ابن الفرس : ( وللشافعي في أحد قوليه أنه لا يجوز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r6.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r6.claim: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal permits proxy pilgrimage and does not require the person to repeat it if the impediment later ends.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r6.anchor: ومذهب أحمد بن حنبل جوازه ولا تجب عليه إعادة الحج إن زال عذره .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r7.speaker: ابن الجلاب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r7.claim: Ibn al-Jallāb says hiring someone to perform pilgrimage for an incapable person is disliked, but an agreement made is not annulled.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r7.anchor: قال ابن الجلاب في ( التفريع ) يكره أن يستأجر من يحج عنه فإن فعل ذلك لم يفسخ )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r8.speaker: ابن القصار
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r8.claim: Ibn al-Qaṣṣār permits proxy pilgrimage for the dead but not for a permanently incapacitated living person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r8.anchor: وقال ابن القصار : ( يجوز ذلك في الميت دون المعضوب ) ( وهو العاجز عن النهوض ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r9.speaker: ابن حبيب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r9.claim: Ibn Ḥabīb says a son may perform pilgrimage for a deceased person even without a bequest, and reports a concession for an elderly person unable to travel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r9.anchor: وقال ابن حبيب : ( قد جاءت الرخصة في ذلك عن الكبير الذي لا ينهض وعن الميت أنه يحج عنه ابنه وإن لم يوص به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r10.speaker: ابن عرفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r10.claim: Al-Abbī reports that Ibn ʿArafa once purchased a proxy pilgrimage for Sultan Abu al-ʿAbbās al-Ḥafṣī according to a school opposing Mālik's.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r10.anchor: ذكر أن الشيخ ابن عرفة عام حج اشترى حجة للسلطان أبي العباس الحفصي على مذهب المخالف )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r11.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r11.claim: Mālik rejects proxy prayer, fasting, and pilgrimage for the dead, preferring other gifts such as alms or freeing a slave; al-Bājī distinguishes these from financial spending.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r11.anchor: فسئل مالك عن الحج عن الميت فقال : ( أما الصلاة والصيام والحج عنه فلا نرى ذلك ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r12.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r12.claim: One Shāfiʿī opinion says the reward of voluntary prayer and other voluntary acts does not reach the dead.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r12.anchor: وقال الشافعي في أحد قوله : لا يصله ثواب الصلوات التطوع وسائر التطوعات .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r13.speaker: صاحب التوضيح
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r13.claim: The Shāfiʿī author of al-Tawḍīḥ says their stronger opinion permits deputizing for a voluntary pilgrimage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r13.anchor: وعندنا يجوز الاستنابة في حجة التطوع على أصح القولين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r14.speaker: أحمد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r14.claim: Aḥmad says the reward of prayers and all other voluntary acts reaches the dead.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p136/r14.anchor: وقال أحمد : ( يصله ثواب الصلوات وسائر التطوعات ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r1.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r1.claim: The well-known Shāfiʿī position says Quran recitation and gifting its reward do not benefit the deceased.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r1.anchor: والمشهور من مذهب الشافعي : أن قراءة القرآن وإهداء ثوابها للميت لا يصله ثوابها ،

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r2.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r2.claim: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and many Shāfiʿī scholars say the reward of gifted Quran recitation reaches the deceased.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r2.anchor: وقال أحمد بن حنبل وكثير من أصحاب الشافعي : يصله ثوابها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r3.speaker: ابن الفرس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r3.claim: Ibn al-Faras reports that Mālik's school permits gifting Quran recitation's reward to the deceased and says they benefit from it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r3.anchor: وحكى ابن الفرس عن مذهب مالك : أن من قرأ ووهب ثواب قراءته لميت جاز ذلك ووصل للميت أجره ونفعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r4.claim: The author rejects as unsubstantiated the attribution, in rival legal books, of a blanket ban on gifting recitation's reward to Mālik.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r4.anchor: فما ينسب إلى مالك من عدم جواز إهداء ثواب القراءة في كتب المخالفين غير محرر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r5.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that when the Prophet became gravely ill, she recited the two protective sūras over him and placed his hand on his body for blessing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r5.anchor: ورد في حديث عائشة قالت : ( كان رسول الله يعوذ نفسه بالمعوذات فلما ثقل به المرض كنت أنا أعوذه بهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r6.claim: The author treats ʿĀʾisha's recitation as deputizing in the Prophet's protective recitation, and asks why proxy recitation's reward should not likewise count.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r6.anchor: فهل قراءة المعوذتين إلا نيابة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما كان يفعله بنفسه ، فإذا صحت النيابة في التعوذ والتبرك بالقرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r7.claim: Hajj may be hired as a proxy act because spending is integral to it; prayer and fasting, whose performers cannot take wages, apparently cannot be hired by proxy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r7.anchor: فأما الحج فقد ذكروا فيه جواز الاستئجار بوصية ، أو بغيرها ، لأن الإنفاق من مقومات الحج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r8.claim: Acts for which wages are lawful, such as Quran recitation, can be delegated; the Prophet approved payment for al-Fātiḥa as healing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r8.anchor: وأن القرب التي يصح أخذ الأجر عليها يصح الاستئجار على النيابة فيها مثل قراءة القرآن ، فقد أقر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فعل الذين أخذوا أجرا على رقية الملدوغ بفاتحة الكتاب .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r9.claim: The author says this verse states a former law; those who do not bind Muslims by prior law find no conflict with reports that allow deputized acts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r9.anchor: فقوله تعالى : { وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى } هو حكم كان في شريعة سالفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r10.claim: Those who treat earlier law as binding reconcile the reports with the verse by claiming a special exception, specification, or abrogation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r10.anchor: منهم من أعمل عموم الآية وتأول الأخبار المعارضة لها بالخصوصية ، ومنهم من جعلها مخصصة للعموم ، أو ناسخة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r11.claim: Other harmonizations read the verse as denying reliance on another's work, take saʿy as intention, or read the lām as ʿalā: a person bears no one else's sins.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p137/r11.anchor: ومنهم من تأول ظاهر الآية بأن المراد ليس له ذلك حقيقة بحيث يعتمد على عمله ، أو تأول السعي بالنية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p138/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p138/r1.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p138/r1.claim: Asked by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāhir how multiplied reward fits this verse, al-Ḥusayn answers: one earns one's own deed by justice, while God may multiply it by grace.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p138/r1.anchor: فقال الحسين : معناه أنه ليس له إلا ما سعى عدلا ، ولي أن أجزيه بواحدة ألفا فضلا .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r1.claim: These clauses are coordinated to the initially understood أن in verse 38; the majority read fatḥa, while Abū al-Sammāl reads kasra from verse 42 onward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r1.anchor: وقوله بعد ذلك وأنه، وأنه معطوف كل ذلك على أن المقدرة أولا في قوله: «أنه لا تزر
