IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r3.claim: A report ascribed to Ibn ʿAbbās calls this abrogated by the verse about joining believing offspring to their parents; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects the attribution and abrogation since this is a report and naskh’s conditions are absent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أن قوله: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى منسوخ بقوله: والذين آمنوا واتبعتهم ذريتهم بإيمان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says the rule applied to Abraham’s and Moses’s peoples, while this community may benefit from others’ effort; Saʿd’s charity for his mother is evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: كان هذا الحكم في قوم إبراهيم وموسى، وأما هذه الأمة فلها سعي غيرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r5.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r5.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says الإنسان here means the unbeliever; the believer gets his own effort and what others do for him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r5.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: «الإنسان» الذي في هذه الآية هو الكافر وأما المؤمن فله ما سعى وما سعى له غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r6.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl says justice grants only what one earned, while God’s grace may add what He wills; the governor accepted this answer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r6.anchor: فقال ليس له بالعدل إلا ما سعى، وله بفضل الله ما شاء الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r7.claim: The majority consider the verse to remain in force.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r8.claim: The key is the lām: strict entitlement is only what one earned; mercy, intercession, righteous relatives, multiplied deeds, and forgiveness are grace, not strict entitlement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r8.anchor: إذا حققت الشيء الذي هو حق الإنسان يقول فيه لي كذا لم يجده إلا سعيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r1.claim: Some use the verse to deny posthumous action for another through body or wealth; others distinguish them, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya says both benefit the doer and are credited for the recipient, as in the Prophet’s order to Saʿd to give charity for his mother.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r1.anchor: وهي عندي كلها فضائل للعامل وحسنات تذكر للمعمول عنه، وقد أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سعدا بالصدقة عن أمه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says this teaching is also in the scrolls of Moses and Abraham.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج هذا في صحفهما أيضا ومعناه ليس للإنسان إلا جزاء سعيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r2.claim: A person receives only the recompense of his own effort: good for good deeds and evil for evil deeds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r2.anchor: ومعناه ليس للإنسان إلا جزاء سعيه إن عمل خيرا جزي عليه خيرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was abrogated by 52:21, since children enter Paradise through their parents’ righteousness; Ibn al-Jawzī rejects this because both texts are reports and reports cannot be abrogated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r3.anchor: أحدها أنها منسوخة بقوله وأتبعناهم ذرياتهم بإيمان الطور 21 فأدخل الأبناء الجنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says the rule applied to Abraham’s and Moses’ peoples, whereas this community receives the benefit of its own and others’ deeds; he cites the Prophet’s instruction to perform pilgrimage for a deceased father.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r4.anchor: وأما هذه الأمة فلهم ما سعوا وما سعى غيرهم قاله عكرمة واستدل بقول النبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r5.claim: The Prophet told a woman whose father died without performing pilgrimage: ‘Perform it for him.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r5.anchor: للمرأة التي سألته إن أبي مات ولم يحج فقال حجي عنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r6.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas takes ‘the human’ here to mean an unbeliever; a believer may receive the reward of his own effort and of effort done for him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r6.anchor: المراد بالإنسان ها هنا الكافر فأما المؤمن فله ما سعى وما سعي له قاله الربيع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r7.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl says the verse states what justice requires; by grace, God may increase a person’s reward as He wills.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r7.anchor: ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى من طريق العدل فأما من باب الفضل فجائز أن يزيده الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r8.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r8.claim: Abū Bakr al-Warrāq says what a person strives for means what he intends.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r8.anchor: والخامس أن معنى ما سعى ما نوى قاله أبو بكر الوراق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r9.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r9.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī says an unbeliever has only the good he did in worldly life, where he is recompensed so that none remains for the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r9.anchor: ليس للكافر من الخير إلى ما عمله في الدنيا فيثاب عليه فيها حتى لا يبقى له في الآخرة خير ذكره الثعلبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r10.claim: One grammatical view treats the lām as meaning ‘upon,’ yielding: a person is owed only what he strove for.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r10.anchor: والسابع أن اللام بمعنى على فتقديره ليس على الإنسان إلا ما سعى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r11.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله الزاغوني
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r11.claim: Al-Zāghūnī says a person has only his own effort, though its means vary: he may secure kin, a child, or a friend who prays for him, or serve religion and worship and gain the love of religious people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80#2/r11.anchor: حكى القولين شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله الزاغوني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r2.claim: Just as no one bears another's sin, a person receives reward only for what he or she earned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r2.anchor: أي: كما لا يحمل عليه وزر غيره، كذلك لا يحصل من الأجر إلا ما كسب هو لنفسه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r3.speaker: الشافعي ومن اتبعه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r3.claim: Al-Shafi'i and his followers infer that the reward of Qur'an recitation cannot be gifted to the dead because it is not their act; the Prophet did not recommend it, no Companion transmitted it, and devotional acts require textual authorization rather than analogy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r3.anchor: ومن وهذه الآية الكريمة استنبط الشافعي، رحمه الله، ومن اتبعه أن القراءة لا يصل إهداء ثوابها إلى الموتى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir says supplication and charity do reach the dead, by consensus and explicit scriptural evidence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r4.anchor: فأما الدعاء والصدقة فذاك مجمع على وصولهما، ومنصوص من الشارع عليهما.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r5.claim: The Prophet says a person's deeds cease at death except for a righteous child who prays, continuing charity, or knowledge that benefits others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا مات الإنسان انقطع عمله إلا من ثلاث: من ولد صالح يدعو له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir says these three exceptions remain the deceased's own striving: a waqf is an effect of his work, published knowledge is his work, and a teacher of guidance shares in followers' rewards; 36:12 records deeds and their traces.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r6.anchor: فهذه الثلاثة في الحقيقة هي من سعيه وكده وعمله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r7.claim: A hadith says a man's best food is from his own earnings and that his child is part of his earnings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r7.anchor: كما جاء في الحديث: "إن أطيب ما أكل الرجل من كسبه، وإن ولده من كسبه"

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r14.claim: Only a person's own striving benefits him.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r14.anchor: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى أي: لا ينفع إلا بعمله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r5.claim: إلا ما سعى means only a person's own effort.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r6.claim: Another's effort helps only when based on the deceased's own faith and good conduct, making it effectively their effort.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r6.anchor: أحدهما : أن سعى غيره لما لم ينفعه إلا مبنيا على سعي نفسه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r7.claim: His second answer is that another's deed does not benefit if done for oneself, but if intended for the deceased sacred law treats the performer as their agent.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r7.anchor: والثاني ؛ أن سعي غيره لا ينفعه إذا عمله لنفسه

MUQATIL:53:33-42/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r7.claim: In the Hereafter, each person has only what they did in worldly life.
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r7.anchor: { وأن ليس للإنسان } في الآخرة { إلا ما سعى } [آية: 39] يعني إلا ما عمل في الدنيا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#2/r1.claim: A person has only his own effort; this statement too occurs in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#2/r1.anchor: الا سعيه وهذه ايضا مما في صحق إبراهيم وموسى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#2/r2.claim: Authentic reports say charity for the dead and pilgrimage on their behalf benefit them: another's effort counts as theirs when based on their own faith and causal role, or when legally intended for them as an agent or proxy.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#2/r2.anchor: واما ما صح في الاخبار من الصدقة من الميت والحج عنه فقد قيل ان سعى غيره لما لم ينفعه الا مبنيا على سى نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says this is abrogated by the promise to join believing descendants with parents; children may enter a parent's scale and intercede for one another.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنها منسوخة بقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas adduces the inheritance verse: people do not know which parents or children will benefit them more.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r2.anchor: يدل على ذلك قوله تعالى آباؤكم وأبناؤكم لا تدرون أيهم أقرب لكم نفعا

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r3.speaker: أكثر أهل التأويل
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r3.claim: Most exegetes consider it un-abrogated: no one's deeds benefit another, and they agree no one performs prayer for another.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r3.anchor: وقال أكثر أهل التأويل: هي محكمة ولا ينفع أحدا عمل أحد

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r4.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r4.claim: Malik disallows fasting, pilgrimage, and charity for the dead, but permits a proxy pilgrimage if stipulated in a will.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r4.anchor: ولم يجز مالك الصيام والحج والصدقة عن الميت

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r5.speaker: الشافعي وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r5.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and others permit voluntary pilgrimage on behalf of the deceased.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r5.anchor: وأجاز الشافعي وغيره الحج التطوع عن الميت

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r6.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r6.claim: A report says ʿA'isha performed retreat and freed a slave for her brother ʿAbd al-Rahman.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r6.anchor: وروي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها اعتكفت عن أخيها

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r7.speaker: سعد بن عبادة عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r7.claim: Saʿd ibn ʿUbada asked whether he could give charity for his dead mother; the Prophet said yes and named water as best.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r7.anchor: أن سعد بن عبادة قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن أمي توفيت

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r8.claim: The genitive lām denotes ownership or obligation, so only one's own striving is owed to oneself.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r8.anchor: لام الخفض معناها في العربية الملك والإيجاب فلم يجب للإنسان إلا ما سعى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r9.claim: God may still favor the deceased with another's gift, as He admits children to Paradise without deeds of their own.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r9.anchor: كما يتفضل على الأطفال بإدخالهم الجنة بغير عمل

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r10.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r10.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas limits this to disbelievers; believers receive their striving and what others do for them.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r10.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: { وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى } يعني الكافر

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r11.claim: Al-Qurtubi says many hadith support believers receiving others' good deeds, and charity is undisputed, citing Ibn al-Mubarak in Muslim.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r11.anchor: وكثير من الأحاديث يدل على هذا القول، وأن المؤمن يصل إليه ثواب

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r12.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r12.claim: A sound hadith says deeds cease at death except three continuing sources, including a righteous child praying for the deceased.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r12.anchor: إذا مات الإنسان انقطع عمله إلا من ثلاث

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r13.claim: Multiplying good deeds from tenfold to seven hundredfold and beyond is divine generosity.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r13.anchor: كما أن زيادة الأضعاف فضل منه كتب لهم بالحسنة الواحدة عشرا إلى سبعمائة ضعف

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r14.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r14.claim: A question asked Abu Hurayra whether the Prophet said one good deed could earn a millionfold reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39/r14.anchor: كما قيل لأبي هريرة: أسمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi suggests the verse may concern evil deeds specifically, based on the hadith distinguishing good and evil intentions.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r1.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون قوله: { وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى } خاص في السيئة

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r2.claim: A sound Muslim report says an unperformed good intention is recorded as good, an accomplished good is multiplied up to seven hundred, and an accomplished evil is recorded once.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r2.anchor: قال الله عز وجل إذا هم عبدي بحسنة ولم يعملها كتبتها له حسنة

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r3.claim: Al-Warraq interprets striving as intending, supported by the saying that people are resurrected according to their intentions.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: { إلا ما سعى } إلا ما نوى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r4.claim: The just baseline is that each person has only their own striving, though multiplied rewards are divine favor.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r4.anchor: فهذا تفضل. وطريق العدل { وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى }.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra answered that he heard the Prophet promise two millionfold reward for one good deed.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:39#2/r5.anchor: إن الله ليجزي على الحسنة الواحدة ألفي ألف حسنة

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r10.claim: People's striving differs: worldly pursuit loses, pursuit of Paradise profits, disciplining the self reaches God's approval, and striving in spiritual aspiration is thanked by God and guided to Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r10.anchor: الناس في سعيهم مختلفون ؛ فمن كان سعيه في طلب الدنيا خسرت صفقته ، ومن كان سعيه في طلب الجنة ربحت صفقته

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r11.claim: A sinner who strives to seek forgiveness and regrets the darkening of his record will receive reward, nearness, honor, and intimacy from God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r11.anchor: وأما المذنب - فإذا كان سعيه في طلب غفرانه ، وندم القلب على ما اسود من ديوانه ، فسوف يجد من الله الثواب والقربة والكرامة والزلفة

TAB-FULL:v22p79/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r3.claim: A person is recompensed only for their own deeds, good or bad, so no worker receives another's reward or punishment.
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r3.anchor: يقول جل ثناؤه: أولم ينبأ أنه لا يجازى عامل إلا بعمله، خيرا كان ذلك أو شرا

TAB-FULL:v22p79/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the phrase in the chapter of the Night as meaning people's deeds.
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى} [النجم: 39]

TAB-FULL:v22p79/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was abrogated by the verse stating that believing descendants are joined to their righteous forebears.
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله {وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى} [النجم: 39] قال: «فأنزل الله بعد هذا (والذين آمنوا وأتبعناهم ذرياتهم بإيمان ألحقنا بهم ذرياتهم)
